A_target.statement: The category of [[Definition:Boolean Algebra|Boolean algebras]] is [[Definition:Dual Equivalence of Categories|dually equivalent]] to the category of [[Definition:Stone Space|Stone spaces]], that is, [[Definition:Compact Space|compact]] [[Definition:Totally Disconnected Space|totally disconnected]] [[Definition:Hausdorff Space|Hausdorff spaces]], with continuous maps.

B_source.statement: The points of a space can be represented as [[Definition:Homomorphism (Abstract Algebra)|homomorphisms]] from an algebra of functions on it to the two-element algebra $\mathbf 2$.

substitutions.a point of the space: a homomorphism from the algebra to the two-element algebra
substitutions.an element of the algebra: the clopen set of points where it evaluates to true
substitutions.an algebra homomorphism: the continuous map in the reverse direction

derived.the space attached to an algebra: its space of ultrafilters, with the topology generated by those clopen sets
derived.the reversal of direction: algebra maps induce continuous maps the other way, by composition

object_map.reformulation: Recover the space from the algebra by taking points to be homomorphisms, which reverses the direction of every map.

validity_conditions: Homomorphisms to the two-element algebra correspond to ultrafilters, so the space of points can be built purely from the algebra.
The construction is contravariant because a homomorphism is composed with rather than applied to a point, which reverses the direction.
Compactness and total disconnectedness of the resulting space are exactly what is needed for the correspondence to be a bijection on both sides.
proof_plan: For a Boolean algebra $B$, let $\map S B$ be the set of homomorphisms $B \to \mathbf 2$, equivalently the [[Definition:Ultrafilter|ultrafilters]] of $B$.

For $b \in B$ let $U_b = \set {x \in \map S B: \map x b = 1}$.
The $U_b$ form a [[Definition:Basis (Topology)|basis]] of [[Definition:Clopen Set|clopen]] sets, making $\map S B$ a Stone space by [[Tychonoff's Theorem]] applied to $\mathbf 2^B$.

A homomorphism $h: B \to B'$ induces $\map S h: \map S {B'} \to \map S B$, $x \mapsto x \circ h$.
As $\map {\map S h^{-1} } {U_b} = U_{\map h b}$, $\map S h$ is continuous, and the direction is reversed.

Conversely, a Stone space $X$ gives the Boolean algebra of its clopen sets.
By the [[Stone Representation Theorem]], $b \mapsto U_b$ is an isomorphism, and each Stone space is homeomorphic to the space of ultrafilters of its clopen algebra.
Hence the constructions are mutually inverse.
{{qed}}
